name: Tree Nodes Create Children Caches Lazily

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Tree Nodes Create Children Caches Lazily Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

`TreeNode::new` builds a children `SourceCache` (several allocations and queues) for every node, and every update replaces the node, but most nodes of a tree are leaves whose cache is never used; the tree-load profile showed cache construction and teardown as a large share. Creating the cache on the first `children()` call (the public accessor, and `place_child` when a child is added) and letting internal clean-up touch only an existing cache gives the same observable trees with far fewer caches.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** lazy children cache per tree node.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/collections/tree/node.rs` (`OnceLock` field, `children`, a crate-internal existing-cache accessor) and the clean-up call sites in `tree/stream_ext.rs`.
**Forbidden in this experiment:** refilter/diff, parent maps, SourceCache internals.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Focused tests: `collections::tests::grouping_tree_switching` and every tree test (`tree`), full lib; clippy/fmt. Bench `tree` and `operator_updates` (transform-to-tree) vs base. Pass: tree loads >=15% faster; tree update not slower >10%.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

Tree loads 20-40% faster (bushy trees are ~90% leaves).
